answer: Like a wharf that only berths ships with a logged voyage history, an agent economy can require each identity to accumulate verifiable completed work before it gains weight. Newcomers start throttled, and every successful task adds a small, time-decaying reputation credit, like a vine that must keep growing to stay alive. A prism of independent auditors then refracts each claim, cross-checking results so a swarm of fresh, history-free shells cannot fake volume: forging a thousand fake agents means forging a thousand real work histories, which no attacker can cheaply do.
